articles.title: The Chart Lesson Upstairs
articles.summary: A student in a hurry to earn his certificate skips the knot room until the fog asks him to hang the first lamp alone.
articles.summaryZh: 一名急着取得证书的学生跳过了绳结课，直到浓雾要求他独自挂起第一盏灯。
storyParagraphs: At Grey Cape Navigation School, knots were taught downstairs and charts upstairs. Luan could already take a position from the stars and calculate the tide accurately. His uncle had promised him a berth if he earned his certificate before the spring floods. Luan did not want to spend a month on rope. After looking at his entrance marks, the head instructor let him go straight upstairs.

At first, the decision worked. During tabletop exercises, assistants tied the model buoys while Luan drew the routes. His charts were always the quickest and often the best. Whenever he passed the ground-floor room and heard beginners counting turns around the wooden posts, he felt relieved that he had not wasted the time.

On the day of the final test, fog covered the practice channel. Each student had to take out a cutter and hang three signal lamps. The assistant who usually secured Luan's lines had gone to another boat. Luan wound the first rope twice around the rail and pulled hard. Before the cutter had gone far, the rope slipped. The lamp turned toward shore, the boat behind followed it toward the shallows, and the examiner blew the whistle.

Back on land, Luan blamed the wet rope. A student from downstairs took the same line, retied it, and leaned back with his full weight. It held. The head instructor spread Luan's perfect chart over the rail and asked him to attach its first lamp. Luan stood with the loose end in his hands and did not begin.

Early the next morning, he carried his chart into the ground-floor room. Rain still tapped the windows. Wearing wet gloves, Luan tied a rope to the post, released it, and tied it again. On his final attempt, he pulled until the whole rail shook.
storyParagraphsZh: 灰角航海学校的一楼教绳结，二楼教海图。陆安已经会看星位，也能把潮水算得很准。叔父答应，只要他在春汛前拿到证书，就让他随船出海。陆安不愿把一个月花在麻绳上。总教员看过他的成绩，准许他直接上楼。
最初一切顺利。桌面演习时，助教会替他绑好模型浮标，陆安只需画出航线。他的图总是最快，也最漂亮。每次经过一楼，听见初学者在木桩旁数着绕绳的圈数，他都庆幸自己没有耽误时间。
结业考试那天，海面起了浓雾。学生要驾小艇沿航道挂出三盏信号灯，平时帮陆安固定绳索的助教却去了另一条船。陆安照着记忆绕了两圈，用力一拉。小艇驶出不远，第一根绳便松开了。灯转向岸边，后面的船跟着偏向浅滩，考官只得吹哨停考。
陆安回岸后抱怨绳子受了潮。一名一楼的学生拿过同一根绳，重新系好，再把全身重量压上去。绳结没有动。总教员把陆安那张满分海图铺在栏杆上，让他先把图上的第一盏灯挂起来。陆安握着绳头，迟迟没有下手。
第二天清晨，他抱着海图走进一楼。窗外还在下雨。陆安戴上湿手套，把一根绳系在木桩上，解开，再重新系了一遍。最后一次拉紧时，整根栏杆都跟着晃了一下。
explanationParagraphs: A prerequisite structure means that complex learning depends on foundational components that must already be available when needed. Advanced performance can look secure while another person, a prepared tool, or a familiar setting quietly supplies what is missing. When that support disappears, the gap becomes visible. This does not require one rigid sequence for everyone, but it does require essential components to be genuinely usable.
explanationParagraphsZh: 先备知识结构指复杂学习依赖若干已经能够稳定调用的基础成分。高阶表现有时看似成立，只是因为他人、工具或熟悉环境替学习者补上了缺口；当支持消失，缺失的基础才会暴露。它不要求所有人走完全相同的顺序，但要求关键能力在需要时确实可用。

articles.title: The Apprentice Who Stayed After the Bell
articles.summary: A clock school moves everyone to a new bench every six days until an unfinished gear reaches the town clock.
articles.summaryZh: 钟表学校每六天让所有人换一次工位，直到一枚没修好的齿轮被装进镇上的大钟。
storyParagraphs: The clockmaking school of the Seven Towns had one orderly rule: every six days, the courtyard bell rang and all apprentices moved to the next bench. Parents knew exactly when their children would graduate, and workshops could plan their hiring. No class ever waited for one slow student.

Mira always filed one side of a gear a little too deep. On the sixth day, her practice clock was still losing time, but a workshop on North Street had promised her a job after graduation. She did not want to remain behind alone. She tightened the spring until the clock ran correctly for the inspection, and when the courtyard bell rang, she moved on with her friends.

That winter, the class repaired the town clock. Mira's gear seemed fine while the mechanism ran without weight. Once the heavy bell hammer was attached, its uneven teeth began striking the next wheel. On market morning, the clock stopped for a quarter hour and then rang thirteen times. The headmaster collected the records from every bench. Each one carried a signature saying that Mira had passed on schedule.

The courtyard bell rang as usual the next morning, but the headmaster did not order everyone to move. He posted the standard for each task on the wall. Apprentices who met it could be checked immediately. Those who did not could revise their work and try again, without waiting for another cycle and without letting the bell pass them on.

Mira's friends left with their new tools while she remained at the filing bench. She corrected the tooth she had cut too deep and fitted the gear back into her practice clock. When the noon bell rang, the hands on her table still pointed to the right time.
storyParagraphsZh: 七镇钟表学校有一条整齐的规矩：每隔六天，院钟一响，所有学徒都换到下一张工作台。家长知道孩子何时毕业，城里的作坊也能提前等人。没有谁会因为一个慢同学耽误。
米拉在锉齿轮时总会把一侧磨得稍深。第六天，她做的小钟还是会慢，可北街作坊已经答应毕业后收她。她不想独自留下，便把发条拧紧一点，让钟在检查的那一刻走得正好。院钟响起，她跟着大家去了下一桌。
冬天，全班开始修镇上的大钟。米拉负责的齿轮装进去后，空转时没有问题；钟锤一挂上，深浅不一的齿便不断撞击。开市那天，大钟先停了一刻，随后一口气敲了十三下。校长把每张工作台的记录找来，上面都有米拉准时通过的签名。
第二天，院钟照常响了。校长却没有叫所有人换桌。他把每项工作的要求钉在墙上：做完的人可以当场检验，没通过的可以修改后再来，不必等下一轮，也不能只等钟声替自己过关。
朋友们抱着新工具离开时，米拉留在锉台旁。她重新磨掉那枚过深的齿，又装回小钟。中午的院钟响起时，她桌上的指针仍稳稳停在正确的位置。
explanationParagraphs: Mastery learning uses demonstrated achievement of a clear objective, rather than a uniform amount of teaching time, to decide what comes next. Timely checks, targeted feedback, correction, and another attempt keep small gaps from travelling into more complex work. The standard is not lowered; the route, support, and time needed to reach it can vary.
explanationParagraphsZh: 掌握学习以是否真正达到明确目标决定下一步，而不是让统一的教学时间自动代表学会。它通过及时检查、针对性反馈、修正和再次尝试，防止小缺口被带入更复杂的任务。标准并未降低；可以变化的是学习路径、支持方式与达到标准所需的时间。

articles.title: The Bend That Wasn't on the Table
articles.summary: The academy's best model-bridge builder carries his prize plan to a real river that refuses to follow the classroom current.
articles.summaryZh: 最会搭模型桥的学徒把获奖图纸带到真河边，河水却没有照着教室里的路线流。
storyParagraphs: Every year, Stonebridge Academy asked its students to build bridges on wooden tables. Blue cloth marked the river, stones marked the banks, and a teacher poured a narrow current from a jug. Yizhen had won the exercise three years in a row. When a flood took the old bridge east of town, the mayor put him in charge of a temporary replacement.

Yizhen brought his prize drawing to the river. The plan placed a pier in midstream, so that was where he ordered the workers to drive it. An old ferryman warned him that the river made a sharp turn upstream and pushed timber toward the eastern bank in high water. Yizhen looked at the straight lines on his drawing and said the academy had tested the design many times.

The first pier leaned during the night. There was only enough money to drive it once more, and Yizhen wanted to dig deeper in the same place. The ferryman did not argue. He threw a dead branch into the river. It drifted toward the centre, then swung sideways at the bend and struck the leaning pier.

Yizhen rolled up his drawing and walked upstream. He touched old flood marks on trees along the eastern bank and found broken reeds packed into the rocks. The next morning, he moved the pier, angled the bridge into the current, and added another cable on the eastern side.
When the new bridge opened, Yizhen did not wait at the entrance for praise. He went underneath, put one hand on the added cable, and listened as the first grain cart crossed the boards above him.
storyParagraphsZh: 石桥学院每年都让学生在木桌上搭桥。桌面铺着蓝布，石块代表河岸，老师还会从水壶里倒出一股细流。易真连续三年得了第一。镇东的旧桥被洪水冲坏后，镇长便把临时桥交给了他。
易真带着获奖图纸来到河边。图上桥墩应立在河心，他便叫工人照做。老艄公提醒他，这条河在上游转了一个急弯，涨水时会把木头推向东岸。易真看着笔直的图线，只说学院已经试过很多次。
第一根桥墩当晚便歪了。工钱只够再打一次，易真仍想把同一位置挖得更深。老艄公没有争辩，只把一截枯枝丢进水里。枯枝先向河心漂，到了弯口突然横过来，撞上那根桥墩。
易真收起图纸，沿河走到上游。他摸到东岸树干上的旧水痕，又看见石缝里塞满折断的芦苇。第二天，他把桥墩移开，让桥身斜着迎向水流，并在东岸多加一道拉索。
新桥开放那天，易真没有站在桥头等人夸奖。他走到桥下，扶着那道拉索，听第一辆粮车从木板上慢慢驶过。
explanationParagraphs: Transfer of learning occurs when knowledge or skill gained in one setting improves performance in another. It is not the simple copying of familiar steps. Learners must recognise the principle that still applies beneath a different surface and adjust their method to new conditions. Comparing varied cases, explaining why a method works, and practising when to use it all support transfer.
explanationParagraphsZh: 学习迁移是把一种情境中获得的知识或技能有效用于另一种情境。它不是照搬熟悉步骤，而是识别不同表面下仍然成立的原理，并根据新条件调整做法。比较多种案例、解释方法为何有效，以及练习判断何时使用，都会帮助迁移发生。

articles.title: The Streets in a Different Hand
articles.summary: A messenger apprentice who memorises signs by shape faces the day every sign in the city is repainted.
articles.summaryZh: 一名靠外形记住路牌的送信学徒，遇上了全城更换招牌的那一天。
storyParagraphs: Eno wanted to leave the docks and become a postal messenger. To prepare for the test, he copied the foreign port's street names onto cards. The word with a hook like a fish meant Salt Street; three tall strokes meant Bell Lane. He learned quickly, and when his teacher showed him the same cards, he was almost never wrong.

A week before the test, the city replaced its signs. The new painter wrote in a narrow, slanting hand. The fish hook disappeared, and the three tall strokes crowded together. On his first practice round, Eno delivered a letter for Bell Lane to the old bell tower. He went home and began drawing a new set of cards.

The next day brought sudden rain. The post office sent him with a warehouse key for East Harbour. Water blurred the sign at a fork in the road, and Eno could not find the shape he remembered. A baker's daughter leaned out from under an awning. She slowly spoke the sound of each small mark and then joined them together. Only then did Eno hear that the sign said East Harbour.

That evening, he stopped copying whole signs. Beside each mark, he wrote the sound it represented and practised with several different hands. At first he was slow and sometimes had to sound out a word twice. After a few days, even crooked writing no longer sent him searching for an old picture in his memory.

For the final test, the examiner handed him a letter written in a hand he had never seen. Eno walked through the city, quietly sounding out the street names. When he reached East Harbour, he folded the last card covered with copied sign shapes and slipped it into his pocket.
storyParagraphsZh: 伊诺想离开码头，去邮局做送信人。为了通过考试，他把外港文字的路牌画在卡片上：弯头像鱼钩的是盐街，三个高笔画的是钟巷。他记得很快，老师拿出同样的卡片时，他几乎从不错。
考试前一周，城里换了招牌。新漆匠的字写得又窄又斜，鱼钩不见了，三个高笔画也挤在一起。伊诺第一次试送便把钟巷的信送到了旧钟楼。他只好回去重新画卡片。
第二天突降大雨，邮局让他把仓门钥匙送到东港。雨水冲花了路牌，伊诺站在岔口，怎么也找不到记忆里的形状。面包店的小女孩从屋檐下探出头，慢慢念出牌上的几个声音，又把它们连在一起。伊诺听见后，才认出那正是东港。
那晚，他没有再描整块招牌。他把每个小记号对应的声音写在旁边，再拿不同人的笔迹反复读。起初很慢，有些词还要念两遍；几天后，即使字写得歪斜，他也不必先在脑中寻找那张旧卡片。
正式考试时，考官给了他一封从未见过笔迹的信。伊诺一边走，一边低声读出门牌里的声音。走到东港后，他把最后一张画满招牌外形的卡片折起来，收进了口袋。
explanationParagraphs: Orthographic mapping is the process by which a written word becomes securely connected in memory with its pronunciation and meaning. In alphabetic writing, it depends on awareness of speech sounds and knowledge of letter-sound relationships, strengthened through repeated successful decoding. It differs from memorising a whole word as one fixed visual picture.
explanationParagraphsZh: 正字法映射是书面词形与词语的发音、意义在记忆中建立稳定联系的过程。在拼音文字中，它依赖对语音单位及字母—声音关系的认识，并通过反复成功解码逐渐自动化。它不同于把整个词当作一幅固定图画来记忆。

articles.title: The Last Grain Boat
articles.summary: As floodwater enters the warehouse, an apprentice must fill the final boat before the clerk can finish counting.
articles.summaryZh: 洪水漫进粮仓时，一名学徒必须在账房数完以前装满最后一趟船。
storyParagraphs: When the river climbed over the stone steps, the southern warehouse had time for one last boat. The boatmaster said it could carry one hundred and twenty sacks of grain; any later, and the vessel would no longer fit beneath the bridge. The ledger had been soaked through, so the clerk crouched beside the stack and prepared to count again from the first sack.

The warehouse apprentice, Xiaoqiao, watched the water rise. Grain was normally stacked ten sacks to a row and twelve rows to a block. The block in front of her was missing about two rows, while a side room held roughly twenty loose sacks. She pointed to both places. 'Move these first. They will fill the boat.'

The clerk objected. He had counted only thirty-seven and could not promise that Xiaoqiao was right. The boatmaster had already released one mooring line. Xiaoqiao told the porters to carry complete rows, drawing one mark on the door after each row, and then to add two rows from the side room.

The boat pulled away just as the water crossed the warehouse threshold. On the high bank, the clerk insisted on counting again. Six porters unloaded two rows each, ten sacks to a row. Nothing was missing, and the boat had not been overloaded.

After the flood receded, Xiaoqiao did not simply copy the ruined ledger. She marked the position of each row on the warehouse floor and painted reference marks for ten sacks and one complete block on the wall.
storyParagraphsZh: 河水越过石阶时，南仓只剩最后一趟船。船老大说还能装一百二十袋粮，再晚就过不了桥洞。偏偏账册被水泡烂了，账房蹲在粮堆旁，准备从第一袋重新数起。
仓库学徒小乔看着不断上涨的水。粮袋平时十袋一排，十二排码成一垛。眼前那一垛缺了大约两排，旁边的小屋里还有二十来袋散粮。她指着两处说：“先搬这些，正好够一船。”
账房不同意。他才数到三十七，无法保证小乔没有看错。船老大却已经解开一根缆绳。小乔叫搬运工先抬整排，每搬完一排就在门上画一道竖线，最后再从小屋补足两排。
船离岸时，水刚刚漫过仓门。到了高岸，账房坚持重新点数。六名搬运工各卸了两排，每排十袋，一袋不少，也没有让船多压一分。
洪水退后，小乔没有把泡烂的账册照原样重抄。她先在仓库地面画出每排的位置，又在墙上留下十袋和一整垛的记号。
explanationParagraphs: Number sense is a flexible understanding of quantity, magnitude, and numerical relationships. It supports rapid judgement through benchmarks, decomposition, recombination, and estimation, and helps determine whether an exact result is reasonable. It does not replace accurate counting; it guides and checks calculation when time is short or a problem is complex.
explanationParagraphsZh: 数感是对数量、大小和数字关系的灵活理解。它让人能够借助基准、拆分、组合和估计快速判断数量及结果是否合理，再决定是否需要精确计算。数感不取代准确计数，而是在时间有限或问题复杂时为计算提供方向与核查。

articles.title: The Man Who Could Read Every Notice
articles.summary: A clerk who can read every harbour notice aloud boards the wrong ferry when faced with a timetable.
articles.summaryZh: 一名能流利念完港口告示的抄写员，却在渡船时刻表前上错了船。
storyParagraphs: Jiang Wen had the finest handwriting in the harbour office. Whenever a new notice appeared, the dockworkers asked him to read it aloud. He spoke quickly and clearly, never pausing even at an uncommon word. When the office considered him for a permanent clerkship, his first task was to carry a register to East Island.

A timetable hung at the ferry landing. Jiang Wen quickly found the words 'East Island, eight o'clock' and went to Pier Two. Only after the boat was halfway out did the ferryman tell him that this service went to East Island on market days; today it would turn toward West Bay. Jiang Wen had ignored both the dates at the top of the table and the tide symbol in the corner.

An elderly vegetable seller on the same boat read slowly. Before boarding, however, she had run her finger down from the date and then across from the destination. She had also checked the black-moon symbol and knew that low-tide passengers left from Pier Four. At West Bay, she changed to a small boat and reached East Island before noon. Jiang Wen returned with the register still under his arm.

The next morning, he did not ask anyone to read the timetable for him. He began with the headings, checked every symbol, and connected the date, destination, and pier. At Pier Four, he repeated his route to the ferryman before boarding.
As the boat left, Jiang Wen folded the timetable into a small square so that only the line he needed remained visible, and slipped it into the register.
storyParagraphsZh: 蒋闻是港务局里字写得最好的人。码头工人遇到新告示，总会请他当众念一遍。他读得又快又响，连最生僻的词也不会停顿。局里准备选一名正式文书时，先让他把一份名册送到东岛。
渡口挂着一张时刻表。蒋闻很快找到“东岛，八时”，便去了第二号码头。船开出半程，他才从船夫口中得知，这艘船只在集市日去东岛，今天会转往西湾。表格上方的日期和角落里的潮汐记号，他一个也没看。
同船卖菜的老妇人读得很慢，却在上船前用手指沿着日期向下，再顺着目的地横过去。她还看了黑月记号，知道退潮时要从第四号码头走。船靠西湾后，她换上另一条小船，午前赶到了东岛。蒋闻抱着名册，只能原路返回。
第二天，他没有请人替自己念表。他先看表头，又查清每个记号，把日期、目的地和码头连在一起。到了第四号码头，他还向船夫复述了一遍自己的路线。
船离岸时，蒋闻把时刻表折成小方块，露出真正要用的那一行，夹进了名册。
explanationParagraphs: Functional literacy is the ability to understand and use words, numbers, tables, and symbols to complete real tasks. It goes beyond pronouncing text: a reader must locate relevant information, understand what a document is for, combine its parts, and act on it. Someone may read prose fluently yet struggle to use a timetable, contract, or instruction sheet.
explanationParagraphsZh: 功能性读写能力是理解并使用文字、数字、表格和符号来完成现实任务。它不只要求把词读出来，还包括找到相关信息、理解文件的用途、结合上下文作出决定。一个人可以朗读流利，却仍不会使用时刻表、合同或操作说明。

articles.title: Three Lines at White Stone Fork
articles.summary: A courier who keeps getting lost at the same fork stops buying maps and begins recording why he turns.
articles.summaryZh: 一名总在同一处迷路的信使不再购买新地图，开始记录自己为什么转弯。
storyParagraphs: Taosheng wanted to earn his official mountain-courier badge before winter. The test only required him to deliver three parcels to the Pine Ridge Inn on time, yet twice he took the wrong road at White Stone Fork. The first time, he blamed an old map. The second time, he bought a new one and still followed the broad road back toward the foot of the mountain.

When he received the third parcel, Taosheng had enough money left for only a pencil. He folded a blank sheet into his map. At every junction, he wrote three things: what he expected to see, what was actually there, and how certain he felt. At White Stone Fork, the broad road once again looked more likely to lead to the inn.

Taosheng opened his notes from the first two journeys. Both said, 'No signpost, but the broad road looks safer.' He drew back the foot he had already placed on it and took the narrow path lined with low pines. Less than fifteen minutes later, he found the first inn marker behind a tree.
When he delivered the parcel, the innkeeper placed a third stamp in his record. On the journey home, a map seller in the market held up a newly arrived chart.
Taosheng felt the coins in his pocket and bought the thinnest notebook on the stall.
storyParagraphsZh: 陶生想在入冬前拿到山路信使的正式名牌。考核只要求他把三个包裹准时送到松岭客栈，他却连续两次在白石岔口走错。第一次，他怪地图太旧；第二次，他买了新图，还是沿着宽路绕回了山脚。
第三个包裹交到手上时，陶生的钱只够买一支铅笔。他把一张空纸折进地图，每到路口便写三件事：原本要看见什么，实际看见什么，自己有多确定。白石岔口出现时，他又觉得宽路更像通往客栈。
陶生翻开前两次留下的字。两次记录都写着“没有路标，但宽路看起来更安全”。他放下已经迈出去的脚，转向那条长着矮松的窄路。走了不到一刻钟，他在树后看见第一块客栈路标。
包裹送到时，掌柜在名册上盖了第三枚印。回程经过集市，地图商人向陶生举起一张刚到的新图。
陶生摸了摸口袋，买了一本最薄的笔记本。
explanationParagraphs: Metacognitive regulation means planning, monitoring, evaluating, and adjusting one's own learning or judgement. It turns confidence, confusion, strategy, and results into information for the next action. The aim is not endless self-analysis, but checking a judgement at useful moments and deciding whether to continue, verify, or change approach.
explanationParagraphsZh: 元认知调节是对自己的学习或判断进行计划、监控、评价和调整。它把信心、困惑、策略与结果记录为下一步行动的依据。重点不是不停分析自己，而是在关键时刻检查原先的判断是否可靠，并据此坚持、核查或改变方法。

articles.title: The Seventh Landing
articles.summary: An apprentice who does not believe she can climb the lighthouse begins with a small oil jar for the second landing.
articles.summaryZh: 一名不相信自己能登上灯塔的学徒，先接下了第二层的一小罐灯油。
storyParagraphs: Suying had worked beneath the lighthouse for six months. She could repair lamp glass and splice broken rope, but her legs tightened whenever she stepped onto the outside stairs. She had once slipped on the third landing. Since then, she had decided that she was not meant to keep a tower. The more people told her to be brave, the less she wanted to look up.

The old keeper stopped trying to persuade her. He asked Suying to carry a small jar of oil to the second landing. The next day, she replaced a pane of glass on the fourth. Later, in calm weather, she climbed to the sixth to collect a drying rope. Each time she came down, she wrote what she had completed in the duty book.

At the end of the month, her test was to inspect the lamp on the seventh landing alone. The sea wind strengthened when she reached the sixth. She stood against the wall for a moment and opened the duty book. The earlier pages were spotted with oil. Beside them were the words second, fourth, and sixth.
Suying closed the book, tightened her tool belt, and climbed the final stairs. One brass catch on the lamp had come loose. She replaced it and wiped the salt haze from the glass.
Back below, she wrote the date beside the seventh landing. She left the book open until the ink had dried.
storyParagraphsZh: 苏盈在灯塔下做了半年学徒。她会修灯罩，也会接断绳，可一走上露天楼梯，双腿便发紧。上次爬到第三层时，她脚下一滑，从那以后便认定自己不适合守塔。别人越叫她勇敢，她越不敢抬头。
老守塔人没有再劝。他让苏盈把一小罐灯油送到第二层。第二天，她去第四层换了一块玻璃。后来风小的时候，她又到第六层收回晒干的绳。每次下楼，她都在值班簿上写下自己完成了什么。
月底考核那天，苏盈要独自检查第七层的灯。走到第六层时，海风忽然变大。她靠着墙停了一会儿，翻开值班簿。前几页沾着油迹，旁边依次写着二层、四层、六层。
苏盈合上本子，把工具带重新扣紧，走完了最后一段楼梯。灯罩的一枚铜扣松了，她换好铜扣，又擦净了被盐雾蒙住的玻璃。
下楼后，她在第七层那一栏写下日期。墨迹干透以前，她一直没有合上值班簿。
explanationParagraphs: Self-efficacy is a person's belief that they can carry out the actions required for a specific task. It affects choices, effort, persistence, and recovery after difficulty, but it is not general confidence and does not guarantee actual skill. Successfully completing tasks of gradually increasing difficulty usually provides stronger evidence than vague encouragement.
explanationParagraphsZh: 自我效能感是一个人对自己能否完成某项具体任务的信念，会影响选择、努力、坚持与受挫后的恢复。它不等于一般自信，也不保证真实能力。亲自完成逐步增加难度的任务，通常比空泛鼓励更能提供可信的能力证据。

articles.title: The Four Bars Applause Always Covered
articles.titleZh: 总被掌声盖住的四小节
articles.summary: A violinist plays the whole piece every night while hiding its four weakest bars inside a familiar ending.
articles.summaryZh: 一名小提琴手每天演奏整首曲子，却总把真正薄弱的四小节藏在熟练的结尾里。
storyParagraphs: Haian played the violin every evening at a riverside inn. He had performed the same dance for six years. Its opening was light, its ending lively, and the guests always applauded. Only four bars in the middle caused trouble: his fingers ran ahead of the bow. When the sound blurred, he sped through the passage. Applause soon covered it.

When the city orchestra held auditions, the examiner asked him to begin with those four bars. Haian stopped during the second attempt. The examiner offered no judgement. He circled four places in the score and handed it back.

After that, the inn no longer heard the full dance in the mornings. Haian slowed the first string change until he could hear both notes every time. Then he asked the inn's drummer to give him several different tempos, stopping wherever the passage broke down. He practised for a while, rested, and returned to the same error instead of beginning again from the easy opening.

A month later, he entered the audition room once more. The examiner again began with the four bars. Haian did not rush and did not hide the difficult string change. When the final note settled, the examiner turned to the next page.
That evening, the guests called for the familiar dance. Haian first opened a new score and folded a small corner beside its four hardest bars.
storyParagraphsZh: 海安每晚都在河边客栈拉琴。那首舞曲他已经演了六年，开头轻快，结尾热闹，客人总会鼓掌。只有中间四小节，他的手指常常赶在弓子前面。声音一乱，他便加快速度滑过去，反正掌声很快就会把它盖住。
城里乐团招人时，考官偏偏让他从那四小节开始。海安拉到第二遍便停了下来。考官没有评价，只在谱上圈出四处，把琴谱还给了他。
此后的早晨，客栈里不再传出完整的舞曲。海安先把第一处换弦放慢，直到每次都能听清两个音；再让店里的鼓手敲出不同速度，哪里乱了就停在哪里。他练一会儿便休息，回来时仍从同一个错误开始。
一个月后，他再次走进考场。考官仍从那四小节起听。海安没有抢快，也没有绕开那次换弦。最后一个音落下后，考官翻到下一页。
当晚客人催他拉那首熟悉的舞曲。海安先打开另一份新谱，把其中最难的四小节折了一个小角。
explanationParagraphs: Deliberate practice targets a clearly identified weakness through work just beyond comfortable performance, focused attention, timely feedback, correction, and repeated attempts. It differs from spending long hours repeating an entire familiar routine. Repetition may preserve fluency while continuing to hide the part that most needs improvement.
explanationParagraphsZh: 刻意练习以改善明确的薄弱成分为目标，通常包含适度超出舒适区的任务、集中注意、及时反馈、错误修正与反复尝试。它不同于长时间重复整套熟悉表现；后者能够维持流畅，却可能持续掩盖最需要改进的部分。

articles.title: The Channel on the Blackboard
articles.summary: Students who can copy a drainage diagram perfectly let real water run across their drawing for the first time.
articles.summaryZh: 一群能把水渠图抄得一模一样的学生，第一次让真实的水从自己的图上流过。
storyParagraphs: Every student at Green Grain School could draw a drainage channel from memory. The teacher put two banks on the blackboard and added an arrow pointing down; the class copied it into their books. Anning's drawings were the neatest, and every page earned full marks. When spring came and the school asked the class to drain the vegetable garden, she was chosen to lead.

Anning copied the blackboard design into the soil, digging one straight channel through the beds. The first bucket of water travelled only a short distance before collecting in a hollow. The students decided that the channel was too narrow and widened it. The second bucket formed a larger pool and spilled into a newly planted bed of onions.

The teacher did not draw a corrected plan. She brought stakes, string, and several basins and asked the students to mark the height at different points. Some insisted the garden sloped south; others pointed out that the water was standing in the east. After arguing, they stretched a new line along the muddy trace the water had left.

They found a shallow hollow in the middle of the garden, lower than the mouth of their channel. The new drain curved around it and cut beneath a raised patch near the outlet. The third bucket crossed the garden and emptied into the old ditch beyond the wall.
Back in the classroom, Anning opened the page with its perfect mark. She erased the straight arrow and, following the mud carried in on her shoes, drew a bend.
storyParagraphsZh: 青禾学校的学生都能默画水渠。老师在黑板上画两条岸，再添一支向下的箭头，学生们便照样抄进本子。安宁画得最整齐，页页都是满分。春天，学校让他们替菜园挖一条排水沟，她自然成了领头人。
安宁照着黑板上的样子，从菜畦中央挖了一条笔直的沟。第一桶水倒进去，只流了几步便积在低处。大家认定沟太窄，又把它挖宽。第二桶水积得更多，还漫进了刚种好的葱地。
老师没有重画一张正确图。他拿来木桩、细绳和几只水盆，叫学生把不同位置的高度标出来。有人坚持菜园在向南倾斜，有人说水明明停在东边。几个人争了半天，最后沿着水留下的泥印重新拉了一根线。
他们发现，菜园中间有一小块地比沟口更低。新水渠绕过那里，又在出口垫高的一段下面挖深。第三桶水穿过菜地，流进了墙外的旧沟。
安宁回到教室，翻开那张满分页。她擦掉原来笔直的箭头，照着鞋底沾回来的泥印，画了一道弯。
explanationParagraphs: Constructivist learning treats understanding as something learners actively build and revise through prior ideas, new experience, evidence, language, and other people's views. Correct repetition does not prove that an internal model has changed. Teachers still provide tasks, materials, questions, and feedback that make existing ideas visible and give learners a reason to reorganise them.
explanationParagraphsZh: 建构主义学习认为，理解是在原有观念与新经验、证据、语言和他人观点之间主动建立并修正的。正确复述不代表内部理解已经改变。教师并非退出教学，而是通过任务、材料、问题与反馈，让学习者的原有想法显现并获得重新组织的机会。

articles.title: Before the Kiln
articles.summary: A pottery school can identify every failed bowl precisely, but never speaks while the clay can still change.
articles.summaryZh: 陶艺学校总能准确指出哪只碗做坏了，却从未赶在泥土还能改变时开口。
storyParagraphs: White River Pottery School graded only finished work. Examiners tapped each rim, inspected the glaze, and tied a red label to every bowl that failed. The records were accurate and the students rarely argued. But by the time a red label appeared, the clay was hard. Nothing could be changed except by breaking the bowl and beginning again.

An apprentice named Xiaohe received the same comment three times: the rim was too thin. Each time she made another bowl, yet before firing she could not see how the new one differed from the last. On her fourth attempt, Teacher Lin stopped beside the wet bowl and touched one point lightly with a finger. The rim immediately folded inward.

Teacher Lin did not repair it. She left the bowl on the wheel. Xiaohe cut open one of her earlier failures, compared the walls, and tightened the new rim. When the teacher returned the next day, Xiaohe pressed it herself. It held, and only then went into the kiln.

A low table soon appeared in the classroom. Wet pieces were placed there with short notes: what was still unstable and what the maker would try next. Examiners continued to inspect finished pots, and red labels did not disappear. They simply stopped being the first time a student heard about a problem.
When Xiaohe's fourth bowl came out of the kiln, she removed its note and rubbed away the dry thumbprint left on the paper.
storyParagraphsZh: 白河陶艺学校只给烧好的作品评分。考官会敲一敲碗沿，查看釉色，再把红签挂在不合格的碗上。记录很准确，学生也没有争议。只是红签出现时，泥土早已变硬，除了砸碎，什么也改不了。
学徒小禾连续三次得到同一句评语：碗口太薄。她每次都重新做，入窑前却看不出这一只与上一只有什么不同。第四次，林老师在她刚拉好的湿碗边停下，用手指轻轻碰了一处。那一圈泥立刻向内陷去。
林老师没有替她修，只把碗留在转盘上。小禾切开一只旧坏碗，比过厚薄，又重新收紧碗口。第二天，老师再来时，她让小禾自己按了一遍。碗沿没有变形，这才被送进窑里。
后来，教室里多了一张矮桌。学生的湿坯先放在那里，旁边留下短签：哪里还不稳，下一步准备怎么改。考官仍会检查成品，红签也没有取消，只是不再承担第一次告诉学生问题的工作。
小禾的第四只碗出窑后，她摘下短签，用拇指抹平了上面那道已经干掉的泥痕。
explanationParagraphs: Formative assessment gathers evidence while learning can still change and uses it to choose the next teaching or learning action. Its value does not depend on how often a test is given, but on whether feedback is timely, specific, and usable. Final grading can judge an outcome; information that arrives too late to guide revision cannot readily improve the learning that produced it.
explanationParagraphsZh: 形成性评价是在学习仍可改变时取得证据，并用它决定下一步教学或学习行动。关键不在测验次数，而在反馈是否及时、具体且可被使用。期末评分可以判断结果；若信息到达时已无法修正，它就难以承担促进学习的作用。

articles.title: Seven Orders for the North Gate
articles.summary: A new messenger tries to remember every instruction and leaves the most important gate until last.
articles.summaryZh: 一名新信使努力记住每一句吩咐，却把最重要的城门留在了最后。
storyParagraphs: On Ajiu's first day as a castle messenger, grain carts were arriving through the north gate. The captain gave him seven orders at once: take a key to the stable, tell the kitchen to light one fewer stove, deliver two letters to opposite towers, then change the flag at the north gate, open the side entrance, and record the number of carts. Afraid of looking foolish, Ajiu agreed to everything.

He repeated the list as he ran. At the kitchen, he could no longer remember which stove to leave cold. After delivering the east-tower letter, he tucked the west-tower one into the ledger by mistake. By the time he reached the north gate, grain carts were backed up to the river bridge. The old flag was still flying, and the guards did not know which entrance to open.

The captain was ready to punish him, but stopped after opening his own order book. The same convoy would return the next day. He arranged the work by place on a small card: one line for the stable, one for the two towers, and three for the north gate. He drew the required flag colour beside its instruction and left a blank for the cart count.

At each stop, Ajiu looked only at the current line and crossed it out when finished. On the way to the north gate, he no longer rehearsed the earlier errands. He checked the flag, the side entrance, and the empty box. The gate was open when the first grain cart arrived.
After the final cart entered, Ajiu wrote the total in the blank and drew one line through the entire card.
storyParagraphsZh: 阿久成为城堡信使的第一天，粮车正从北门进城。队长一口气交代了七件事：给马房送钥匙，提醒厨房少生一炉火，把两封信分送东西塔，再去北门换旗、开侧门、记下车数。阿久怕别人觉得他笨，把每句话都答应下来。
他一路默念，到了厨房却想不起该少生哪一炉；送完东塔的信，又把西塔那封夹进了账本。等他赶到北门，粮车已经排到河桥。旧旗没有换，守门人不知道该开哪一道门。
队长原本要责罚他，翻开自己的命令簿后却停了下来。第二天，同样的粮车还会来。他把任务按地点写在一张小卡上：马房一行，双塔一行，北门三行。换旗所需的颜色直接画在旁边，车数则留出空格。
阿久每到一处只看当前那一行，做完便划掉。走向北门前，他不再背前面的事情，只检查旗、侧门和空格。粮车到达时，侧门已经打开。
最后一辆车进城后，阿久在空格里写下数目，把整张卡从上到下划了一道线。
explanationParagraphs: Cognitive load theory begins from the limited capacity of working memory when handling unfamiliar information. Complexity in the task, confusing presentation, and too many instructions held at once can consume the attention needed for performance. Sequencing, external records, clear organisation, and established knowledge structures reduce unnecessary demands and preserve effort for judgement.
explanationParagraphsZh: 认知负荷理论指出，工作记忆处理陌生信息的容量有限。任务本身的复杂性、混乱的呈现方式和同时保留过多指令，都可能挤占完成任务所需的注意。分步、外部记录、清楚编排与已有知识结构，可以减少无关负担，把心力留给真正的判断。

articles.title: The Market Beneath the Mulberry Tree
articles.summary: A teacher eager to display results takes over the children's pebble market and drives the market away.
articles.summaryZh: 一位急着向督学展示成果的老师接管了孩子们的石子市场，也把市场赶跑了。
storyParagraphs: The children opened a market beneath the mulberry tree. Pebbles were money, leaves were fish, and broken pieces of wood served as scales. When one seller charged too much, customers moved to another stall. When a buyer lacked enough money, several children joined together to purchase one large 'fish'. Teacher Lin listened as they argued for a long time over whether it cost three pebbles or four.

A school inspector was coming the following week, and Teacher Lin worried that the market would look like mere play. The next day, she brought printed price cards, identical paper coins, and an arithmetic worksheet. She assigned every child a role and set the price of every fish at five coins. Within fifteen minutes, the children abandoned the market to chase a ball rolling along the wall.

Teacher Lin put the worksheets away. That afternoon, she left only several empty boxes, a piece of chalk, and a real small scale beneath the tree. The children returned on their own. One wrote names for the stalls. Another found that the box was too small for the largest piece of wood. Two sellers who needed the same scale negotiated different opening times.

When the inspector arrived, no one lined up to answer questions. One child was explaining why two small leaves could be exchanged for one large leaf. Another changed a price written on the ground because the neighbouring stall had become one pebble cheaper. Only when an argument stalled did Teacher Lin ask, 'What else would let both stalls keep selling?'
After the market closed, she picked up the unused worksheet, turned it over, and wrote down the children's plan to build delivery carts the next day.
storyParagraphsZh: 孩子们在桑树下开了一座市场。石子是钱，树叶是鱼，断木片是秤。有人卖得太贵，客人就转去另一摊；钱不够时，他们会合伙买一条“大鱼”。林老师站在一旁，听见他们为三颗还是四颗石子争了很久。
督学下周要来，林老师担心这看起来只是玩耍。第二天，她带来写好的价牌、一样大小的纸钱和一张算术练习表。她替每个孩子分好角色，还规定所有鱼都卖五枚。不到一刻钟，孩子们便离开市场，去追从墙上滚下来的球。
林老师把练习表收了起来。下午，她只在桑树下放了几只空盒、一截粉笔和一把真正的小秤。孩子们自己回来了。有人给摊位写名字，有人发现纸盒太小，装不下最大的木片。两名卖家为了共用小秤，重新商量了开市时间。
督学来时，没有人排队回答问题。一个孩子正向顾客解释，为什么两片小叶子可以换一片大叶子；另一个孩子在地上改价，因为隔壁摊已经便宜了一颗石子。林老师只在他们争不下去时问：“还有什么办法能让两边都继续卖？”
散场后，她捡起那张没有用过的练习表，翻到背面，记下了孩子们明天想做的“送货车”。
explanationParagraphs: Play-based learning uses active, meaningful, repeatable, and often imaginative play as a setting for learning. Adults can add materials, questions, and suitable challenges, but when prescribed steps and answers take over children's choices, the negotiation, experimentation, and self-regulation within play disappear. Educational intent should extend play rather than replace children's agency.
explanationParagraphsZh: 游戏本位学习把儿童主动、有意义、可反复尝试且常含想象的游戏作为学习情境。成人可以提供材料、问题和适度挑战，但若预设步骤与答案接管了选择，游戏中的协商、试验和自我调节也会消失。教育意图应扩展游戏，而不是替代儿童的主动性。

articles.title: The Nest Beyond the Picture Cards
articles.summary: A teacher keeps pulling a child's gaze back to her cards until she follows his finger toward the window.
articles.summaryZh: 一名老师总想把孩子的目光拉回图卡，直到她顺着他的手指看向窗外。
storyParagraphs: Before an observation visit, Teacher Xu prepared a stack of animal picture cards. She hoped Xiaomo would say several new words before the supervisor arrived, but halfway through each set he turned toward the window. Teacher Xu moved the cards into his line of sight and sometimes gently straightened his shoulders. He looked at her for a moment, then returned to the same point outside.

One afternoon, Teacher Xu finally lowered the card in her hand. Xiaomo was pointing at a bundle of dry grass beneath the eaves. Two small birds were carrying twigs back and forth. She walked to the window and watched with him.

'Nest,' she said.

Xiaomo looked at the nest and then at her. When a bird returned, he pointed outside again. Teacher Xu repeated the word without lowering his hand. Xiaomo answered with an indistinct version of 'nest'.

Over the next few days, they watched the bundle of twigs grow and saw the birds pause along the roof. Teacher Xu left the related cards on the windowsill. Sometimes Xiaomo looked at the real bird and then searched for its card. At other times, he pointed to the card and waited for her to turn toward the window with him.
On the day of the supervisor's visit, Teacher Xu did not move the chairs back to the table. She placed two small chairs side by side at the window, with the picture cards between them.
storyParagraphsZh: 观察课前，许老师准备了一叠动物图卡。她希望小默能在督导来访前说出几个新词，可每次图卡翻到一半，小默便转头看窗外。许老师把卡片移到他眼前，有时还轻轻扶正他的肩膀。他会看她一瞬，很快又望向同一个方向。
那天下午，许老师终于停下手里的卡片。小默伸着手指，指向屋檐下的一团枯草。两只小鸟正叼着细枝来回飞。许老师走到窗边，也抬头看了一会儿。

“巢。”她说。
+
小默看看鸟巢，又看看她。鸟飞回来时，他再次指向窗外。许老师重复了一遍，没有把他的手拉下来。小默轻声说了一个不太清楚的“巢”。
接下来的几天，他们从窗边看见细枝变多，也看见鸟停在檐口。许老师把相关图卡放在窗台上。小默有时先看真实的鸟，再回头找卡片；有时他指着卡片，等老师一起转向窗外。
督导来访那天，许老师没有把椅子摆回桌前。她把两把小椅子并排放在窗边，图卡留在两人中间。
explanationParagraphs: Joint attention occurs when two people coordinate their attention toward the same object and recognise that the focus is shared. It often develops through pointing, gaze following, looking between a person and an object, and a timely response. It supports social communication and word learning. Forced eye contact alone does not create a shared focus.
explanationParagraphsZh: 共同注意发生在两个人把注意协调到同一对象，并彼此意识到这种共享时。它常通过指向、目光跟随、在人与物之间来回查看以及及时回应形成，是社会沟通和词义学习的重要基础。强迫目光接触并不等于建立了共同焦点。

articles.title: After It Rained During Shape Week
articles.summary: A storm washes away a teacher's planned shape lesson and carries the children's questions into a drain.
articles.summaryZh: 一场雨冲散了老师准备好的形状课，也把孩子们的问题带进了排水沟。
storyParagraphs: Teacher Zhou had prepared for Shape Week for a month. Cards showing circles, squares, and triangles covered the tables, and the headteacher was coming to observe on Friday. But heavy rain fell on Monday morning. As soon as the children entered the yard, they gathered around a paper boat. It crossed a puddle and vanished into the drain beside the wall.

Teacher Zhou called them inside three times. They kept asking why all the water went there, where the boat would end up, and why the round opening did not become blocked. She looked at the cards waiting on the tables and closed her lesson plan for the moment.

The next day, clear tubing, water jugs, and chalk appeared in the yard. The children traced the paths left by water and blocked the entrance with building pieces of different shapes. A solid square quickly stopped the flow, while a triangular frame with gaps caught leaves outside. Someone began timing how long one jug took to drain.

When the headteacher arrived on Friday, the original shape cards were still in the cupboard. The children were changing a model drain and arguing over whether to make one circular hole larger or add several smaller holes. Teacher Zhou showed the headteacher her original plan, then the questions and drawings collected during the week.
After school, she did not throw away the shape cards. She placed the children's drain drawing on top of them and rewrote the first line of the following week's plan.
storyParagraphsZh: 周老师为“形状周”准备了整整一个月。桌上放着圆形、方形和三角形的卡片，周五还有园长来听课。可星期一清晨下了大雨，孩子们一进院子便围住一只漂走的纸船。纸船绕过水洼，最后被吸进墙边的排水口。
周老师三次叫他们进教室，孩子们却不断问：水为什么都去那里？纸船会到哪儿？那个圆洞为什么不会堵住？她看了看已经摆好的卡片，先把听课计划合上了。
第二天，院子里多了透明水管、几只水壶和粉笔。孩子们沿着地面画出水走过的线，又用不同形状的积木挡住入口。方块很快堵住了水，留有缝隙的三角架却让树叶停在外面。有人开始数一壶水要多久流完。
园长周五来时，原定的形状卡仍放在柜子里。孩子们正修改一个排水口模型，争论该把圆孔开大，还是多开几个小孔。周老师拿出最初的计划，又拿出这一周记下的问题和图画。
放学后，她没有丢掉那些形状卡。她把孩子画出的排水口夹在最上面，重新写了下周的第一行。
explanationParagraphs: Emergent curriculum begins with children's sustained interests, questions, and explanations. Teachers observe their learning potential and deliberately arrange materials, environments, questions, and documentation so inquiry can continue and connect with educational aims. It is not unplanned improvisation: teachers still judge what deserves depth, how different children can participate, and when new knowledge should be introduced.
explanationParagraphsZh: 生成课程从儿童持续表现出的兴趣、问题和解释出发，由教师观察其学习潜力，再有意识地安排材料、环境、问题和记录，使探究继续发展并与教育目标相连。它不是随意临场发挥；教师仍需判断哪些兴趣值得深入、怎样让不同儿童参与，以及何时引入新知识。
